messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Forwarding rule API error rate spike detected in GCP eu-west1. Affects ILB route propagation for Private VPC customers. Auto-severity: P1. Paging oncall @jamal. Ticket opened with GCP (CASE-11327).
jamal: on it. seeing route_update_latency ~120s for cross-region propagations. Some customers report 502s when failing over between regions. taking initial triage.
maria: which subset of customers? customer impact? any big ones on Dedicated or Private that we should escalate to CS / AMs now?
jamal: Private VPC only so far, mostly EU <-> US cross-region failovers. 3 customers showing elevated 502 rates and route flap. backend healthchecks still ok; problem seems to be forwarding-rules / target-proxy updates not propagating.
chris: observability shows a lot of Cloud Logging 429s during the same window. could be unrelated quota but timing lines up.
elaine: also seeing a spike of 401s from our observability agent to our auth proxy when it tries to push logs to Cloud Logging. token refresh rate increased 30x.
jamal: timeline: 2178456789 alert -> route update latencies spike -> 2178456830 first customer 502 -> 2178456900 logging 429s + auth 401s. putting a short runbook: 1) mitigate customer-facing routing 2) reduce chatter to GCP controlplane 3) engage GCP support.
jamal: mitigation step A: enable region-level static fallback for severely impacted customers to avoid dynamic cross-region reprop. This is temporary — performs an immediate static route and avoids ILB controlplane patch.
jamal: command I'm running (internal ctrl plane):

```
# apply static fallback for customer foo-corp
redwoodctl routes set-static --customer foo-corp --region eu-west1 --force --note "temp fallback 2178456789"
```

maria: nice. can you list which customers you applied to and estimated RTO?
jamal: applied to foo-corp and bar-saas. expected <60s to flip; monitoring shows traffic rebalanced to local regional pools.
chris: to reduce load on GCP forwarding API, we should pause non-urgent rolling updates for customers in privvpc for next 30 min. I'm disabling autosync on the controlplane for the affected region.
elaine: also throttling our observability agents to batch more and drop debug-level logs for the next 15 min. reduces token churn.
jamal: engaged GCP support, they confirm elevated API error rates on Forwarding Rule service in eu-west1. GCP assigned CASE-11327, engineers investigating. They suggested temporary retry/backoff and reducing write rate.
gcp-support-bot: GCP update @jamal: Forwarding Rule API has elevated 5xx and 429s. Engineering is looking at internal controlplane problems. ETA unknown. We recommend regional fallbacks and avoid mass concurrent updates.
maria: outreach: CS team notified two impacted customers privately and opened support threads. AMs notified for any billing/contract escalations.
jamal: paging: handing off to chris for the next 2h window. will make a follow-up summary before leaving.
pagerduty-bot: Handoff: @jamal -> @chris (2h) | incident P1 | see thread 2178456789 | escalation level 2
chris: taking over. running cluster-level policy to force route_fallback for customers in eu-west1. also creating temporary rate-limit in controlplane for forwarding-rule writes to 2r/s.
chris: command:

```
redwoodctl infra set-rate-limit --target forwarding_rule_write --region eu-west1 --rate 2/s
```

elaine: quick log snippet from agent showing 401s when posting logs to cloud logging:

```
2026-03-15T12:13:45Z observ-agent[pid=8245]: POST https://logging.googleapis.com/v2/entries:write -> 401 Unauthorized (token_expired)
2026-03-15T12:14:01Z observ-agent[pid=8246]: POST https://logging.googleapis.com/v2/entries:write -> 429 Too Many Requests
```

chris: we've scaled back logging and set agents to batch every 30s. should reduce token churn and API writes.
jamal: customer impact summary so far: 3 Private VPC customers saw transient cross-region failovers resulting in 1-2 minute service degradation for some endpoints (elevated 502s). No data loss. No hosted API customers impacted.
maria: good to include in incident notes: which mitigations worked and which didn't (static fallback — good, agent throttling — reduced logs 429s). GCP is still working on root cause of forwarding API instability.
chris: monitoring: added temporary alert for forwarding_rule_api_error_rate > 1% sustained 5m. also added metric for route_propagation_time for privvpc customers.
jamal: will prepare initial incident summary for on-call repo. tag postmortem owners: jamal (triage), chris (mitigation), maria (customer comms), elaine (observability).
elaine: next steps: 1) preserve logs for 72h (we had some 429s but keep what we have) 2) run token refresh audit for observability agents 3) propose controlplane rate-limiter for fw rule writes per-region.
maria: CS/AM outreach: done. customer-facing note drafted and ready to send after final sync with GCP support.
gcp-support-bot: GCP update: Engineering traced to an internal forwarding rule controlplane partition experiencing high GC and request queueing. A fix is being rolled out to the controlplane. We'll update with rollout progress. (CASE-11327)
jamal: thanks. handoff complete. I'll join the postmortem after my shift. chris, you're the lead for next 2h — escalate to infra-sre if recovery stalls.
chris: acknowledged. will post an update in 30m or sooner if regression.
maria: adding reminder to create RFC for a safer fallback mechanism so we don't rely on ad-hoc static routes next time.
elaine: noted — will add observability improvements to tracking.
jamal: closing the active pager for now — moving to monitoring-only once GCP rollout shows stabilization. :white_check_mark:
chris: stabilization observed at 2178457850 — error rates dropped to baseline. leaving monitoring on for 60m. final note: open postmortem ticket PM-5122 assigned.
maria: thanks all. I'll send a short customer follow-up and a slack-wide incident summary once PM postmortem is created.
